html:
The Pandyas were one of the three crowned Tamil dynasties of south India, ruling from Madurai in the far south. On the 700 map they are in their first age of power.

Greek and Roman writers knew of them, and their coast at Korkai was famous for pearls. Their early history is told in Tamil Sangam poetry; see the Tamil kingdoms. Around 590 King Kadungon ended the rule of the Kalabhras, and the Pandyas grew strong again, fighting the Pallavas for the Tamil lands.

The Cholas crushed them in the 10th century, but the Pandyas rose again in the 13th century and briefly ruled most of the Tamil country and even Sri Lanka's north. Marco Polo visited their coast. Raids from the Delhi Sultanate after 1311 broke their power, and later Pandya princes ruled only small lands. See also the Pandya state on later maps.
sum: The Pandyas were one of the three crowned Tamil dynasties of south India, ruling from Madurai in the far south. On the 700 map they are in their first age of power.
